target_vertical: Shopify DTC brands (including those that manufacture/bundle, with raw materials and BOMs)
pricing_model: Tiered subscription based on store revenue; unlimited SKUs, POs, and users on all plans; monthly billing via Shopify Billing
shopify_sync_direction: Bi-directional: pulls products, variants, inventory levels, vendors, and orders from Shopify; pushes inventory updates and PO-derived stock changes back to Shopify locations
shopify_synced_entities: Products, variants, inventory levels per location, orders (historical sales for forecasting), Shopify vendors (auto-mapped as suppliers), product images/metadata
shopify_multi_store_support: Yes — connect unlimited Shopify stores per Prediko tenant; supports inventory consolidation across stores
shopify_variant_option_mapping: Variants/SKUs imported directly from Shopify; SKU-level forecasting and bulk-edit on SKUs and suppliers
shopify_real_time_or_batch: Real-time sync with Shopify for stock levels and orders (vendor positions it as live syncing across connected sources)
shopify_known_limitations: Single-channel: Shopify-only — does not natively pull historical sales/demand from Amazon, Etsy, eBay, Walmart (native Amazon integration on waitlist, not GA as of 2026-05). Users sync those marketplaces' orders into Shopify first if they want any visibility. App reported as complex with learning curve. No native POS depth confirmed.
etsy_native_or_third_party: Not supported natively; users must use a third-party syncing app that posts Etsy orders into Shopify, and Prediko will then only see them as Shopify orders
etsy_order_import: Not supported (workaround: sync Etsy orders into Shopify via third-party app)
etsy_known_limitations: No native Etsy integration; per Prediko help center, Etsy demand is not visible to Prediko's planning engine unless routed through Shopify
amazon_supported: None (native integration on waitlist as of 2026-05)
amazon_synced_entities: None today; native Amazon integration announced as upcoming
amazon_known_limitations: No native Amazon integration GA; Prediko documents Amazon/Walmart/Etsy/eBay as marketplaces that should be synced into Shopify externally for any visibility — historical demand from those channels will not appear in Prediko's forecasts
xero_synced_entities: Purchase Orders from Prediko sync directly into Xero as Bills (eliminates manual bill entry); supplier/contact mapping implied
xero_accounting_sync_mode: PO-to-Bill pass-through (Prediko is not an order-to-cash/sales accounting connector — it does not post sales invoices or summary journals; it focuses on the procurement leg)
xero_known_limitations: [uncertain] — integration is procurement-focused (POs → Bills); sales-side and COGS journal coverage not publicly documented
qb_synced_entities: [uncertain] — no QuickBooks integration documented in public materials; Xero is the primary accounting integration
qb_known_limitations: QuickBooks integration not publicly documented; some third-party comparison articles state Prediko's primary accounting integration is Xero, not QuickBooks
other_ecom_channels: Shopify-only as a sales channel. Other marketplaces (Amazon, Walmart, Etsy, eBay) must be funnelled into Shopify via third-party sync apps; native Amazon connector on waitlist. WooCommerce, BigCommerce, TikTok Shop, Wix, Squarespace, Faire, Square, Magento not natively supported.
bundle_kit_component_decomposition: Yes — supports bundles and kits, and via BOMs the components are tracked; production orders are auto-created when a SKU with a BOM is ordered, decrementing raw materials accordingly
other_accounting_integrations: Xero is the documented native accounting integration. No public evidence of Sage, NetSuite, Zoho Books, MYOB, FreshBooks, or Wave integrations.
bom_support: Yes — manage BOMs for finished goods, including raw materials linked to finished SKUs
multi_level_bom: [uncertain] — documentation describes BOMs of finished goods composed of raw materials; multi-level/nested BOMs not explicitly confirmed
production_orders: Yes — production orders are auto-generated for SKUs with BOMs; supports sending production orders to suppliers/manufacturers and tracking raw material consumption
bin_location_support: [uncertain] — multi-location supported, but bin/aisle-level sub-location tracking not confirmed
multi_warehouse: Yes — multi-warehouse / multi-location stock management with inter-location stock transfers
purchase_orders: Yes — core feature: create, share with suppliers in one click or export, partial receipts, link POs to suppliers; AI-suggested PO drafts based on forecast
supplier_management: Yes — Shopify vendors auto-sync as suppliers and map to products/SKUs; track POs across multiple suppliers; bulk-edit suppliers; supplier lead times factored into reorder timing
ai_demand_forecasting: Yes — core differentiator; AI demand forecasting trained on 25M+ SKUs across 15+ industries; factors seasonality, sales patterns, and history; SKU-level 'stock health' indicators
ai_purchase_order_suggestions: Yes — 'To Buy' tab and smart order recommendations generate PO drafts automatically based on forecasted demand, lead times, and current stock
public_api: Public API available (referenced for enterprise tier custom integrations); detailed REST/GraphQL spec [uncertain]
integration_architecture: Native Shopify app with vendor-built direct integrations (Xero direct); enterprise tier offers custom API/WMS integrations; vendor claims 70+ to 100+ integrations across 3PL/WMS/ecommerce tools
mobile_app: [uncertain] — no native iOS/Android app surfaced in public materials; web app only is likely
sync_frequency: Shopify: real-time / live sync. Xero: triggered on PO creation/update. Other systems: [uncertain].
shipping_carrier_integrations: [uncertain] — Prediko is procurement/forecasting focused, not an OMS/shipping app; carrier integrations not its primary scope
three_pl_integrations: Connects to 3PLs and WMS systems (vendor cites 70+ integrations including 3PL/WMS); specific named partners [uncertain]
capterra_rating: [uncertain] — listed on Capterra but specific star rating/review count not surfaced in searches
notable_customers: [uncertain] — vendor describes customer base as Shopify DTC brands; specific named case studies not enumerated here
last_major_release: Ongoing 2026 product updates published on https://www.prediko.io/product-updates (specific release headline date [uncertain])
last_funding_event: $5M Seed round led by Felix Capital, announced May 2022 (with Zinal Growth / Guillaume Pousaz, HelloWorld, NomadCapital, plus angels from Klarna, Gorgias, Zencargo, Pigment, Ankorstore, Yoobic)
